summary.title: Space Invaders from Scratch - Part 5
summary.one_liner: You learn to add a score counter and draw text and numbers in a C++ game by treating characters as sprites from a bitmap spritesheet.
takeaways: Keep a score variable and increase it when a bullet hits an alien, with points depending on alien type (10 to 40 in the author's version).
Draw text by indexing a 65-character 5x7 ASCII spritesheet starting at space (ASCII 32), offsetting each glyph by one pixel of spacing.
Draw numbers by splitting them into digits with modulo 10 and integer division, then drawing each digit sprite left to right.
Add simple UI elements such as the 'SCORE' and 'CREDIT 00' labels and a horizontal divider line by writing directly to the pixel buffer.
summary.summary: This final part of the Space Invaders from Scratch series adds scoring to a C++ clone with minimal dependencies. The author adds a score variable that rises when an alien is hit, then builds a bitmap-font text renderer that treats each ASCII character (space through backtick) as a 5x7 sprite from a spritesheet. A separate function splits a number into digits with modulo and division and draws each digit from the same sheet. The post ends with HUD labels ('SCORE', 'CREDIT 00') and a divider line, and it notes that alien movement, alien bullets and some collision handling are left for the reader or the author's linked reference code.
